stages.title: Carrier Reports Breakdown
stages.event: Load LD-3051 is traveling from Dallas, TX to Memphis, TN. The carrier reports a mechanical breakdown near Little Rock, AR. Repair completion time is unknown, and delivery is scheduled in four hours.
options: Immediately mark the shipment as delivered.
Verify the breakdown details, current location, repair estimate, and delivery risk with the carrier.
Ignore the situation until the scheduled delivery time.
stages.why: Verify the carrier's report and assess delivery risk before communicating an updated ETA.

stages.title: Delivery Appointment at Risk
stages.event: The carrier confirms the repair may take three hours. The original delivery appointment is now at risk.
options: Notify authorized stakeholders, coordinate receiver acceptance or rescheduling, and document the carrier-reported ETA.
Promise that the shipment will arrive on time.
Change the appointment without contacting the receiver.
stages.why: A revised ETA is not a confirmed appointment. Coordinate with the authorized parties and record the outcome.

stages.title: After-Hours Shift Handover
stages.event: Your shift ends in 15 minutes. The repair is ongoing, and the receiver has not confirmed a new appointment.
options: Close the exception before leaving.
Tell the next shift that everything is fine.
Document verified facts, pending appointment, contact history, escalation status, owner, and next follow-up time.
stages.why: An unresolved shipment exception requires a complete and actionable handover.

cases.name: AI Tracking Error and ETA Conflict

stages.title: AI Tracking Alert
stages.event: Load LD-4082 is traveling from Chicago, IL to Columbus, OH. Automated tracking predicts a two-hour delay, but the carrier previously reported an on-time ETA.
options: Immediately notify the customer that delivery is delayed.
Ignore the automated alert.
Compare GPS timestamps, review the carrier update, and verify the latest shipment status.
stages.why: AI predictions are not verified shipment facts. Conflicting information must be investigated.

stages.title: Conflicting ETA Updates
stages.event: The carrier confirms a revised ETA of 8:30 PM ET, but the automated tracking system still shows 7:15 PM ET.
options: Document the verified carrier update, assess the appointment impact, and flag the conflicting automated ETA according to SOP.
Delete all tracking history.
Assume the automated ETA is always correct.
stages.why: Preserve the audit trail and distinguish the confirmed carrier report from potentially stale automated data.

stages.title: Automated Delivery Confirmation
stages.event: The truck enters the receiver geofence. The system automatically marks the shipment Delivered, but unloading has not started.
options: Close the shipment immediately.
Flag or correct the premature status through authorized procedures, verify unloading, and obtain required delivery evidence.
Delete the shipment record.
stages.why: Geofence arrival does not establish completed delivery. Delivery confirmation and required documentation must be verified.

stages.title: Tracking Signal Lost
stages.event: Load LD-5103 is traveling from Atlanta, GA to Nashville, TN. The tracking platform has not received a GPS ping for 75 minutes. Delivery is scheduled this evening.
options: Mark the load delayed without verification.
Check the last timestamp and location, review tracking health, and contact the carrier using approved channels.
Assume the truck has stopped moving.
stages.why: A missing ping does not prove a delay. Verify the signal issue and shipment movement.

stages.title: Carrier Confirms Movement
stages.event: The carrier reports the truck is moving and provides a current location, but the tracking application still shows an old ping.
options: Record the carrier-reported location with its source and time, troubleshoot tracking, and set the next check.
Replace the old GPS timestamp with a fabricated live ping.
Ignore the tracking outage for the rest of the trip.
stages.why: Maintain an honest audit trail and distinguish manual confirmation from automated tracking.

stages.title: Customer Requests an ETA
stages.event: The customer requests a current ETA while automated tracking is still offline.
options: Promise the original ETA without checking.
Say the truck is lost.
Provide the latest verified carrier-reported ETA with its source, note the tracking limitation, and continue monitoring.
stages.why: Communicate verified information and uncertainty without inventing live tracking data.

stages.title: Missed Check Call
stages.event: Load LD-5204 has an early-morning delivery. The carrier missed a scheduled update and the driver is not answering.
options: Repeatedly call the driver until they answer while driving.
Check available tracking and contact the carrier dispatch or authorized alternate; record attempts.
Immediately report the freight stolen.
stages.why: Use safe, approved contact paths and verify available evidence before escalating.

stages.title: Delivery Window Approaches
stages.event: The last verified position is two hours old. The receiver appointment is approaching and the carrier dispatch has not responded.
options: Escalate per SOP, flag the appointment risk, and request an authorized alternate contact or receiver contingency.
Change the TMS to Delivered.
Wait until the next shift without leaving notes.
stages.why: Time-sensitive exceptions need escalation, documentation, and a contingency plan.

stages.title: Shift Handover
stages.event: Your shift ends before the carrier responds.
options: Delete unsuccessful contact attempts.
Tell the next shift to figure it out.
Record last verified location, attempts, appointment deadline, escalation owner, and next action time.
stages.why: A complete handover prevents the next shift from losing critical context.

cases.name: TMS Status Conflict and CRM Update

stages.title: Premature Delivery Status
stages.event: Load LD-5305 is shown as Delivered in the TMS, but the carrier says the vehicle is waiting at the receiver dock.
options: Close the load and invoice immediately.
Verify the actual delivery milestone and correct or flag the status using authorized procedures.
Delete the shipment and start over.
stages.why: Arriving at a receiver is not proof of completed unloading or delivery.

stages.title: Customer Sees Incorrect Status
stages.event: The customer CRM record contains an automated Delivered notification that may be inaccurate.
options: Document the discrepancy, coordinate an accurate customer correction through approved channels, and preserve the audit trail.
Ignore the customer because the TMS says Delivered.
Tell the customer the POD is signed without seeing it.
stages.why: CRM communications must reflect verified operational facts.

stages.title: Document Closeout
stages.event: The carrier confirms unloading is complete but has not sent the signed POD.
options: Invent a POD number.
Close the shipment with no evidence even if POD is required.
Request the required POD, record the confirmed delivery time and source, and close only when company requirements are met.
stages.why: Final closeout requires the appropriate proof and documentation.

stages.title: Driver ETA Slips
stages.event: Load LD-5406 has a 2:00 PM pickup appointment. The driver reports a breakdown and now expects to arrive at 3:30 PM.
options: Confirm the revised ETA, check shipper receiving rules, and notify the broker or customer according to SOP.
Tell the shipper the truck is already on site.
Cancel the shipment without authorization.
stages.why: An appointment change must be coordinated rather than assumed.

stages.title: Shipper Cannot Accommodate
stages.event: The shipper says the 3:30 PM arrival is too late and no later slot is currently available.
options: Tell the driver to enter the facility anyway.
Request the next authorized appointment, evaluate backup equipment or carrier options, and obtain required approvals.
Change the pickup time in the TMS without confirmation.
stages.why: Use authorized alternatives and assess operational feasibility and cost.

stages.title: Possible Accessorial Charge
stages.event: The carrier asks for TONU after the appointment fails. The contract and responsibility are not yet confirmed.
options: Approve payment immediately.
Reject the charge without reviewing evidence.
Preserve dispatch instructions, timestamps, appointment records, and agreements; route the request for contractual review.
stages.why: TONU eligibility depends on the applicable agreement and facts, not assumptions.

cases.name: Customer Escalation and AI Delay Alert

stages.title: AI Predicts Late Delivery
stages.event: Load LD-5507 is moving from Phoenix, AZ to Las Vegas, NV. An AI tool predicts a missed delivery window, but the latest driver update is older than two hours.
options: Verify fresh tracking and carrier information before treating the prediction as confirmed.
Tell the customer delivery has definitely failed.
Turn off every alert permanently.
stages.why: Predictions trigger investigation; they are not confirmation of an actual delay.

stages.title: Customer Demands Immediate Answer
stages.event: The customer asks whether the receiver appointment will be missed. The carrier reports a revised ETA, but receiver acceptance is not confirmed.
options: Guarantee the receiver will unload.
Share the verified ETA and uncertainty, request receiver confirmation, and document the escalation.
Avoid all communication until tomorrow.
stages.why: Separate verified movement information from unconfirmed appointment acceptance.

stages.title: Escalation Resolution
stages.event: The receiver offers a later appointment subject to customer approval.
options: Book it without approval regardless of instructions.
Tell the carrier to unload at a different facility.
Seek the required approval, confirm the revised appointment, update TMS and CRM records, and hand over outstanding tasks.
stages.why: Coordinate approvals and ensure operational systems reflect the confirmed plan.
